observed_gap: getOpenCodeSessionKey chooses the first truthy explicit session/conversation alias by priority and does not validate agreement between simultaneously supplied aliases.
A request with header x-opencode-session=session-A and body session_id=session-B is silently bound to session-A instead of failing closed.
A whitespace-only explicit header is truthy before trimming, so getOpenCodeSessionKey returns the empty string while hasExplicitSessionId returns true.

The chosen session key controls the per-session gate, durable sessionStore record, upstream chat/thread reuse, account affinity and restart checkpoint namespace; therefore alias disagreement is an identity-safety boundary, not a cosmetic parsing issue.

cases.conflicting_header_and_body: current silently selects session-A; candidate rejects conflict
cases.blank_explicit_header: current key is empty while explicit=true; candidate rejects blank
cases.no_explicit_alias: candidate returns no explicit identity and leaves existing fallback policy separate

required_contract: Resolve all explicit session/conversation aliases through one strict helper before any session mutation, gate acquisition or provider work.
Every present explicit alias must be a non-empty string after normalization.
If more than one explicit alias is present, all normalized values must agree exactly; otherwise return a bounded HTTP 400 invalid-request error.
getOpenCodeSessionKey and hasExplicitSessionId must consume the same validated resolution result so they cannot disagree about whether a durable identity exists.
Do not derive provider account/thread identity from this helper and do not weaken the existing per-session serialization/replay rules.
integration_relevance: A future Notion-to-Qwen adapter may carry its provider-neutral conversation key through one explicit body field while an OpenCode/Codex client or proxy also supplies a session header. Silent priority would attach the child to the wrong durable Qwen namespace instead of exposing the protocol mismatch.
limits: No Qwen product file was changed.
No CircleCI or GitHub Actions was triggered.
No live provider, Notion, Codex, accounts, secrets, Windows or production state was used.
